QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_50

question.text: For comparing two Category II growth-equity AIFs of the same vintage but different distribution pace, which SINGLE metric most robustly captures both realised return AND market-pace context?

explanation.text: The Logic: KS-PME compounds each capital call and distribution using the index return to the valuation date and computes a market-adjusted TVPI. Two funds with different distribution paces are made comparable because KS-PME credits each cash flow by its time-in-market index return. KS-PME = 1 means parity with market; > 1 outperformance. IRR alone is timing-sensitive but not market-adjusted. PIC just measures deployment. Absolute INR ignores fund size and time value. The Trap: Gross IRR reflects cash-flow timing but does not adjust for market conditions. PIC only measures capital deployment. Absolute INR doesn't adjust for fund size or vintage. Note: The workbook supports KS-PME as the market-adjusted listed-index comparison method for Category I/II AIFs and notes that IRR can be distorted by cash-flow patterns.
